parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked whether any of the listed sinks actually invoke a shell or execute an external command. The functions involved (fopen, inet_pton, connect, send_request) are standard library/networking calls that use the supplied arguments as data, not as part of an OS command string.  No system(), exec*, or similar is called, so there is no code path that could interpret the inputs as shell commands.  Consequently, malicious content in the arguments cannot lead to command injection.  The use of untrusted input is correctly handled: fopen just opens a file; inet_pton validates the IP; connect attempts a TCP connection; send_request formats an HTTP request.  None of these paths can be abused to execute arbitrary shell code.
